learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the principles governing the vibratory motion of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of dynamic modeling of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of analysis of mathematical models of vibrating mechanical systems.
Knowledge in determining the natural frequencies of mechanical systems.
Knowledge of the physical quantities used in the Mechanical Vibrations discipline and their units of measurement.
Ability to understand the physical phenomena that lead to the appearance of vibrations in mechanical systems.
Ability to solve vibration problems; to determine the natural frequency/natural frequencies for mechanical systems with one/multiple degrees of freedom.
Acquisition of experimental skills for measuring physical quantities used in the study of vibrations.
Creation of subroutines in computer programs that allow the calculation of natural frequencies of mechanical bodies/systems.

syllabus_topics: Composition of harmonic vibrations: collinear synchronous, collinear of different pulsations, orthogonal of the same pulsation
Fourier analysis of a periodic non-harmonic vibration
Vibrations of mechanical systems with one degree of freedom
Forced damped vibrations produced by harmonic disturbing forces
Vibrations of mechanical systems with two degrees of freedom
Vibrations of mechanical systems with multiple degrees of freedom
Derivation of differential equations using Lagrange's equation
Problems of vector representation of harmonic vibrations (practical)
Vibrations of mechanical systems with one degree of freedom (practical)
Vibrations of mechanical systems with 2 degrees of freedom (practical)
Study of the diagram of a damped vibration
Fourier transform of a non-harmonic periodic function
Determination of critical speeds for a shaft with one rotor
Determination of natural frequencies of a mechanical system with 3 degrees of freedom
assessment_rules: A minimum attendance of 70% at lectures and seminars, and 100% at laboratories is required. All laboratory tasks must be completed. A minimum grade of 5 is required for seminar verification tests. For the written exam, a minimum grade of 5 is required for each of the 4 exam topics. The exam consists of a theory subject with short questions, a synthesis subject with demonstrations, a problem requiring the determination of the natural vibration frequency for a one-degree-of-freedom mechanical system, and a problem for determining the natural frequencies of a two-degree-of-freedom mechanical system.
